tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mission): lock every external WriteDispatchPending/ClearDispatchPending caller (P1, PR #509 tail #1)

dispatchAgent holds AcquireDispatchPendingLock across its whole
match-through-admit sequence, but WriteDispatchPending and
ClearDispatchPending are plain filesystem primitives with no locking of
their own -- correct for dispatchAgent's own internal calls (already
inside the one critical section), but every OTHER caller (mission
dispatch/create, mission release, mission close/abandon, session
purge) ran as a separate process with no such lock, so a selected
pending entry could vanish mid-admission or a fresh write could land
right after a concurrent cleanup scan and leave a released session
bound again.

Adds mission.WithDispatchPendingLock, a thin acquire-run-release
wrapper every external caller now goes through. The primitives stay
unlocked deliberately: a real flock locks an open file description,
not a process, so a self-locking primitive would deadlock dispatchAgent
on its own first inner call (matchDispatchPending's stale-entry clear,
consumeDispatchBinding's post-admission consume).

Confirmed the race red first:
TestWriteDispatchPending_UnlockedDoesNotWaitForConcurrentLockHolder
shows the raw primitive completing immediately while a sibling holds
the lock. TestWithDispatchPendingLock_BlocksUntilRelease pins the fix.

make check green (race detector included); GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64
go build ./... exits 0.
EOF
)"
